tests.label: the presence of binary or boolean representations and specific symbols
should_fire: The field accepts only true or false, stored as 1 or 0.
He set the boolean flag to true before running the check.
near_miss: The form asks only for a name or address, stored as text in a file.
He set the oven dial to high before checking the roast.
tests.basis: Vague bundle of binary, boolean, and unspecified symbols with no single defining pattern.

tests.label: key terms related to genetic traits and population genetics
should_fire: The trait is inherited through a recessive allele passed from both parents.
Allele frequencies in the population shifted over several generations.
near_miss: The recipe is handed down through a family notebook passed from both grandparents.
Song styles in the village shifted over several generations.
tests.basis: Tight scientific domain with distinctive vocabulary such as allele and recessive.

tests.label: themes related to personal struggles and emotional conflicts
should_fire: She lay awake worrying that she had disappointed everyone she loved.
He felt torn between staying for his family and leaving for good.
near_miss: She lay awake planning the route she would drive on Saturday morning.
He felt pleased about staying for his family and cooking for everyone.
tests.basis: Abstract emotional theme with no distinctive surface vocabulary.

tests.label: patterns related to numerical data and structured lists
should_fire: The table lists three columns: name, date, and total for each sale.
Sales were 120 in January, 145 in February, and 160 in March.
near_miss: The story names three characters: a baker, a sailor, and a tailor in town.
Sales were strong in January, stronger in February, and strongest in March.
tests.basis: Surface format pattern of digits and enumerated lists that a feature can track directly.

tests.label: code statements that manipulate arrays or data structures
should_fire: The code adds each new score to the array and sorts it.
She removed the last item from the list and stored it in a variable.
near_miss: The clerk adds each new letter to the tray and sorts it.
She removed the last cup from the shelf and stored it in a cabinet.
tests.basis: Tight programming subdomain with distinctive terms such as array, list, and variable.

tests.label: elements related to data representation and measurement in scientific contexts
should_fire: The temperature was recorded in degrees Celsius at five-minute intervals.
They measured the sample's weight in grams using a calibrated scale.
near_miss: The soup was served in large bowls at five-minute intervals throughout lunch.
They judged the cake's flavor at the fair using a simple scorecard.
tests.basis: Broad bundle of data, representation, and measurement across all of science.

tests.label: special characters and symbols used in programming or mathematical contexts
should_fire: He typed the formula a + b * c into the calculator app.
The code checks if a != b before printing the result %.
near_miss: He typed the words alpha and beta into the search box slowly.
The recipe checks if the soup tastes right before serving the meal.
tests.basis: Concrete surface pattern of actual symbol characters in the text.

tests.label: elements of code and programming constructs
should_fire: The function returns a value after the loop finishes each pass.
She declared a variable and assigned it inside the class.
near_miss: The waiter returns a menu after the guests finish each course.
She opened a notebook and wrote inside the cover.
tests.basis: Extremely broad label covering essentially all programming content.

tests.label: commands or functions related to logging or alerting in programming contexts
should_fire: The system logs an error message whenever the connection drops.
She set an alert to notify the team when disk space runs low.
near_miss: The system prints a receipt whenever the customer pays at checkout.
She set a reminder to notify the team when lunch break runs long.
tests.basis: Tight programming subdomain anchored by distinctive log and alert vocabulary.

tests.label: terms related to health or medical concepts, particularly those involving anatomy and physiology
should_fire: The heart pumps blood through arteries to the rest of the body.
Muscles in the leg contract to bend the knee joint.
near_miss: The pump moves water through pipes to the rest of the house.
Ropes on the sail tighten to bend the wooden mast.
tests.basis: Very broad topic spanning all anatomy and physiology, like the pilot's broad food label.

tests.label: chemical compounds related to lipids
should_fire: Cholesterol and triglycerides are lipids carried in the bloodstream.
Fatty acids form the building blocks of many lipid molecules.
near_miss: Vitamins and minerals are nutrients carried in the bloodstream.
Amino acids form the building blocks of many protein molecules.
tests.basis: Tight chemical domain with distinctive compound names such as triglycerides and fatty acids.

tests.label: links and references to external sources
should_fire: Read more at the link below, which points to the full report online.
According to the source cited at the end, the figures come from 2020 census data.
near_miss: Read more in the chapter below, which covers the full topic in detail.
According to the summary printed at the start, the figures come from our own survey.
tests.basis: Surface discourse pattern of pointing to an outside source, with recognizable link and citation phrasing.

tests.label: technical terms and definitions related to mathematical concepts and computational processes
should_fire: A derivative measures the rate of change of a function at a point.
The algorithm's complexity describes how its running time grows with input size.
near_miss: A thermometer measures the outdoor temperature of a garden at noon.
The recipe's difficulty describes how its cooking time grows with batch size.
tests.basis: Multi-concept bundle joining all of mathematics to all computational processes.

tests.label: phrases indicating emotional engagement or personal reflections
should_fire: I still think about that summer and how much it changed me.
Reading her letter, he felt a lump rise in his throat.
near_miss: I still think about that summer and how much it rained there.
Reading her letter, he noted the date written at the top.
tests.basis: Abstract reflective and emotional phrasing with no distinctive surface marker.

tests.label: specific items, brands, and concepts related to technology or electronics, as well as people and organizations
should_fire: The new iPhone from Apple features a brighter screen and faster chip.
Samsung released a laptop with a longer battery life this spring.
near_miss: The new cookbook from the chef features a brighter cover and shorter chapters.
A local farm released a basket with a longer handle this spring.
tests.basis: Incoherent bundle of tech items, brands, people, and organizations with no single claim.

tests.label: code snippets related to programming logic and control structures
should_fire: The program uses an if statement to check the password before granting access.
A while loop repeats the calculation until the total reaches one hundred.
near_miss: The program uses a login screen to check the password before granting access.
A printed table repeats the calculation until the total reaches one hundred.
tests.basis: Broad code topic covering general programming logic as well as control structures, not a single narrow pattern.

tests.label: specific scientific terms related to biology and medicine
should_fire: The enzyme breaks down proteins inside the cell during digestion.
Doctors found bacteria in the sample and prescribed an antibiotic.
near_miss: The machine breaks down boxes inside the warehouse during sorting.
Cooks found herbs in the sample and prescribed a new recipe.
tests.basis: Broad bundle of two large fields, biology and medicine, with a huge open-ended vocabulary.

tests.label: phrases expressing preferences for sharing or communication
should_fire: I would rather share the news by email than wait until Monday.
She prefers to talk things over in person instead of by text.
near_miss: I would rather send the news by email than wait until Monday.
She manages to talk things over in person instead of by text.
tests.basis: Abstract speech act, expressing a preference, with no fixed wording and two targets, sharing and communication.

tests.label: terms related to programming functions, particularly those dealing with data structures and control mechanisms
should_fire: The function sorts the list and returns the smallest value first.
This function checks each item in the array before updating the counter.
near_miss: The clerk sorts the list and returns the smallest value first.
This worker checks each item in the pile before updating the counter.
tests.basis: Multi-concept bundle of functions, data structures, and control mechanisms across general programming.

tests.label: elements related to electromechanical systems
should_fire: The electric motor drives the gear that opens the automatic door.
A relay switches the current to the solenoid when the button is pressed.
near_miss: The electric light brightens the room that opens the automatic door.
A worker flips the sign to the entrance when the bell rings.
tests.basis: Tight technical domain with distinctive component vocabulary like motor, relay, and solenoid.

tests.label: structured data and elements related to programming or model definitions
should_fire: The model defines each field, its type, and whether it is required.
The data is stored as a table with rows for every customer.
near_miss: The essay defines each term, its origin, and whether it is required.
The data is stored as a pile with boxes for every customer.
tests.basis: Vague bundle of structured data, programming elements, and model definitions with no single pattern.

tests.label: details about individuals' educational backgrounds and professional history
should_fire: She earned a degree in history before working as a school administrator.
He studied engineering at university and then spent ten years in banking.
near_miss: She earned a badge in history before helping at the school fair.
He tended the garden at weekends and then spent ten summers in the shed.
tests.basis: Multi-concept biographical bundle combining education history and career history across many topics.

tests.label: proper nouns, particularly place names and related identifiers
should_fire: They flew from Chicago to Denver before driving into the mountains.
The River Thames flows through London past the old bridges.
near_miss: They flew from one city to another before driving into the mountains.
The wide river flows through the painting past the old bridges.
tests.basis: Narrow form pattern: capitalised place names are a distinctive, closed type of token.

tests.label: instances of significant numerical values or statistics
should_fire: Unemployment fell to 4.2 percent, the lowest rate in five years.
The survey found that 68 percent of voters supported the proposal.
near_miss: Unemployment fell slightly, the lowest level in recent memory.
The survey found that most voters supported the proposal.
tests.basis: Numbers are everywhere and significance is a vague judgement, so the class has no exact boundary.

tests.label: mentions of specific names or terms related to financial or transactional contexts
should_fire: She transferred the payment to Marcus through her checking account.
The invoice lists Greenfield Supplies as the vendor for the delivery.
near_miss: She transferred the parcel to Marcus through her checking account.
The invoice lists Greenfield Supplies as the driver for the delivery.
tests.basis: Vague mix of names and terms tied to a broad financial and transactional context.

tests.label: structured data and programming constructs
should_fire: The program stores the names in an array and loops through each entry.
Each record in the database has a key that links it to a customer.
near_miss: The program stores the names in a drawer and loops through each entry.
Each letter in the drawer has a stamp that links it to a customer.
tests.basis: Broad bundle of structured data with general programming constructs, no single tight pattern.

tests.label: phrases related to statistical measurements and observed data frequencies
should_fire: The average score rose, and the most frequent result was seven.
Researchers measured the frequency of errors across a thousand trials.
near_miss: The overall mood rose, and the common result was praise.
Researchers listened to the loudness of voices across the crowded hall.
tests.basis: Broad academic topic spanning many statistical measures and general data language.

tests.label: specific numerical values or symbols associated with various metrics or measurements
should_fire: The temperature reached 37.5 degrees during the afternoon heat.
His score of 92 out of 100 placed him near the top.
near_miss: The temperature felt warm during the afternoon heat.
His score placed him near the top.
tests.basis: Open-ended class, any number attached to any metric, with no specific value or format named.

tests.label: phrases that indicate comparisons or similarities
should_fire: The new phone is similar to the old one but slightly lighter.
Her voice sounded like her sister's on the recording.
near_miss: The new phone is sitting beside the old one but slightly lighter.
Her voice sounded clear on her sister's recording.
tests.basis: Specific grammatical pattern marked by a small set of comparison words like similar to and like.

tests.label: numerical values and sequences, indicating a focus on data or time-related information
should_fire: The readings were 12, 18, 25, and 31 over the four days.
He counted down from ten to one before opening the door.
near_miss: The readings were low, steady, rising, and high over the four days.
He counted down in his head before opening the door.
tests.basis: Vague class of any numbers or sequences, tied loosely to data or time with no exact boundary.

tests.label: syntax elements related to control structures in programming
should_fire: In the code, an if-else statement chooses which message to display.
The for loop in the program repeats the check for every name.
near_miss: In the code, a print statement chooses which message to display.
The menu in the program repeats the check for every name.
tests.basis: Narrow syntax class with a closed set of control structures: if-else, for, and while.

tests.label: functions related to file and database operations
should_fire: The function opens the file, reads each line, and closes it afterwards.
This function saves the new record into the database table.
near_miss: The function opens the window, reads each line, and closes it afterwards.
This function saves the new record into the shopping basket.
tests.basis: Tight operation set for files and databases, marked by distinctive verbs like open, read, save, and close a record.

tests.label: HTML and web development elements
should_fire: He added a heading tag to the HTML page so the title stood out.
She linked the stylesheet to the webpage to change its colors.
near_miss: He added a heading style to the printed page so the title stood out.
She linked the paint swatches to the mood board to change its colors.
tests.basis: HTML plus all web development is a broad multi-concept domain.

tests.label: names and quotation marks
should_fire: "Maria," he said, "please meet my friend James at the station."
The sign read "Eleanor Park" above the gate where Thomas waited.
near_miss: Maria, he said, please meet my friend James at the station.
The sign read Eleanor Park above the gate where Thomas waited.
tests.basis: Multi-concept bundle of proper names and quotation marks, which need not co-occur.

tests.label: technical terms and code-related concepts
should_fire: The developer fixed a bug in the software after checking the error log.
She updated the database so the application would run faster.
near_miss: The gardener fixed a leak in the hose after checking the water pressure.
She updated the address book so the office would work faster.
tests.basis: Technical terms and code concepts in general is an extremely broad topic.

tests.label: references to scientific kits and assays related to molecular biology
should_fire: She opened the PCR kit to test the DNA sample for the gene.
The lab ran an ELISA assay to measure antibodies in the sample.
near_miss: She opened the chemistry kit to test the water sample for minerals.
The clinic ran a blood pressure test to measure circulation in the patient.
tests.basis: Tight molecular-biology domain with distinctive kit and assay vocabulary like PCR and ELISA.

tests.label: phrases discussing actions or activities related to considerations or decisions
should_fire: Before deciding, she considered all the options for the move.
They weighed the costs before making a final decision on the house.
near_miss: Before leaving, she gathered all the bags for the move.
They counted the boxes before making a final delivery to the house.
tests.basis: Abstract decision-related phrasing with no specific wording or concrete referent.

tests.label: terms related to the evaluation of outcomes
should_fire: The results showed the new method worked better than the old one.
Teachers assessed student progress at the end of the term.
near_miss: The photos showed the new garden looked fuller than the old one.
Teachers counted student books at the end of the term.
tests.basis: Evaluation of outcomes is an abstract function expressed with many unrelated terms.

tests.label: keywords related to paths and resources in a programming context
should_fire: The program loaded the image from the file path in the resources folder.
He set the path variable so the app could find the data files.
near_miss: The cook loaded the ingredients from the shopping list in the kitchen cupboard.
He set the meeting time so the team could find the data room.
tests.basis: Vague keyword set spanning paths and resources, two loosely related programming notions.

tests.label: performance metrics related to software compilation or testing
should_fire: The build took twelve seconds and passed all ninety tests.
Their compiler reported fewer errors and a faster runtime this week.
near_miss: The cake took twelve minutes and pleased all ninety guests.
Their kitchen reported fewer complaints and a faster service this week.
tests.basis: Bundles performance metrics with both compilation and testing, several distinct signal types.

tests.label: terms related to semi-structured data or formats
should_fire: He stored the data in JSON format with keys and values for each record.
She converted the spreadsheet into XML so other programs could read the tags.
near_miss: He stored the data in a plain paragraph with sentences and descriptions for each record.
She converted the spreadsheet into a printed table so other people could read the rows.
tests.basis: Semi-structured formats are a tight set with distinctive names like JSON and XML.

tests.label: phrases that express questions or inquiries about personal opinions and perceptions
should_fire: What do you think about the new park in town?
How did the movie feel to you compared with the book?
near_miss: What is the height of the new tower in town?
How did the movie differ in plot compared with the book?
tests.basis: Bundles questions with opinions and perceptions, an abstract multi-part speech act.

tests.label: references to collections or data structures in programming contexts
should_fire: She stored the names in a list so the program could sort them alphabetically.
In the program, he used a dictionary data structure to map each key to a value.
near_miss: She stored the names in a notebook so the class could sort them alphabetically.
In the library, he used a dictionary reference book to check each word's meaning.
tests.basis: Collections and data structures cover many distinct types with different vocabulary.

tests.label: instances of object-oriented programming methods and attributes
should_fire: In the program, the Car object has a color attribute and a start method.
The student class stores a name and prints a report card when called.
near_miss: In the garage, the car itself has a color paint job and a start button.
The school office stores a name and prints a report card when asked.
tests.basis: Bundles methods and attributes across all object-oriented code, a wide construct class.

tests.label: numeric values and symbols related to data structures or programming syntax
should_fire: The array index started at 0 and the next value was 1.
He entered 42 into the variable and ended the line with a semicolon.
near_miss: The shelf label started at A and the next letter was B.
He entered a name into the form and ended the line with a period.
tests.basis: Bundles numbers and symbols with two different programming referents, data structures and syntax.

tests.label: punctuation marks, especially commas
should_fire: She packed apples, oranges, bread, and cheese for the picnic.
On Tuesday, after the meeting, he drove home, cooked dinner, and called his sister.
near_miss: She packed apples and oranges and bread and cheese for the picnic.
On Tuesday after the meeting he drove home and cooked dinner and called his sister.
tests.basis: Punctuation, especially the comma, is a specific surface pattern a feature can track.

tests.label: semicolon-separated import statements in programming code
should_fire: The Java program began with import statements for the math and file libraries, each ending with a semicolon.
He added another import statement after the first one and separated the statements with semicolons so the compiler would accept them.
near_miss: The Python program began with import statements for the math and file libraries, each on its own line without a semicolon.
He added another import statement after the first one and separated the statements with new lines so the reader could follow them.
tests.basis: A single specific format pattern: import statements separated by semicolons.

tests.label: numeric values and operations related to time
should_fire: The train ride lasted two hours and forty minutes.
She set the timer for 30 seconds before checking the oven.
near_miss: The train ride passed two towns and forty fields.
She set the marker for 30 pages before checking the book.
tests.basis: Bundles numeric values with time operations, covering many number-plus-unit combinations.

tests.label: occurrences of code structure or syntax elements commonly used in programming languages
should_fire: The program used a loop to repeat the instructions until the condition changed.
She added brackets around the block of code so the function would run correctly.
near_miss: The assembly line used a cycle to repeat the steps until the product changed.
She added brackets around the block of text so the paragraph would stand out clearly.
tests.basis: Code structure and syntax elements in general covers nearly all programming constructs.

tests.label: references to licensing information and URLs associated with software or documents
should_fire: He downloaded the software under a Creative Commons license from the project website.
The document included licensing information and a link to the source website.
near_miss: He downloaded the software as a free trial from the project website.
The document included cooking information and a link to the source website.
tests.basis: Licensing notices are formulaic with distinctive license names, paired with URL references.

tests.label: error-handling statements and expressions in the context of programming
should_fire: Wrap the file read in a try block and catch the exception if it fails.
The function throws an error when the input is null and logs the failure.
near_miss: Wrap the file read in a loop and repeat the operation if it pauses.
The function returns a value when the input is null and saves the result.
tests.basis: Tight programming subdomain with distinctive vocabulary like try, catch, exception, and throws.

tests.label: punctuation marks, particularly periods
should_fire: Dr. Patel arrived at 3 p.m. and reviewed the chart.
The package came from the U.S. office, e.g. the branch in Ohio.
near_miss: Doctor Patel arrived at three in the afternoon and reviewed the chart.
The package came from the American office, for example the branch in Ohio.
tests.basis: Specific punctuation pattern, with periods inside abbreviations, that is directly present or absent in the text.

tests.label: key information related to mobile application development
should_fire: Building a mobile app for Android requires testing on many screen sizes.
The iOS app sends push notifications when a new message arrives.
near_miss: Building a desktop program for Windows requires testing on many screen sizes.
The web page sends email alerts when a new message arrives.
tests.basis: Broad development topic with vague wording about key information, not a tight distinctive pattern.

tests.label: references to Google's libraries and frameworks
should_fire: The team built the model in TensorFlow, a machine learning library from Google.
She used Angular, the Google framework, to build the web interface.
near_miss: The team built the model in PyTorch, a machine learning library from Meta.
She used Vue, the community framework, to build the web interface.
tests.basis: Narrow set of named Google products like TensorFlow and Angular with distinctive proper names.

tests.label: timestamps related to data entries or logs
should_fire: The log entry was recorded at 2024-06-18 09:14:22 and marked as complete.
Each row in the database carries a timestamp of 15:42:07 from that morning.
near_miss: The log entry was recorded on a Tuesday in June and marked as complete.
Each row in the database carries a note about the weather from that morning.
tests.basis: Specific date-and-time format that appears as a concrete, recognizable token pattern.

tests.label: references to software projects and their attributes
should_fire: The open-source software project released version two with a faster interface.
Their software project has fifty contributors and a public issue tracker.
near_miss: The community garden project planted row two with a faster growing variety.
Their neighborhood project has fifty volunteers and a public sign-up sheet.
tests.basis: Very broad and vague category covering almost any software project and any attribute.

tests.label: conjunctions that express contrast or exception
should_fire: She wanted to go outside, but it started raining hard.
Everyone was invited except Tom, who had to work late.
near_miss: She wanted to go outside, and it started raining hard.
Everyone was invited including Tom, who had to work late.
tests.basis: Small set of specific contrast and exception words like but and except.

tests.label: financial figures and monetary amounts related to significant events or transactions
should_fire: The company was acquired for $2.3 billion in a deal announced Monday.
Investors paid $450 million for the startup during the funding round.
near_miss: The company was featured for two full pages in a story published Monday.
Spectators filled 450 seats for the concert during the opening night.
tests.basis: Concrete monetary amount format, with dollar figures tied to transactions, that is directly visible in the text.

tests.label: phrases or sections of code
should_fire: This section of code loops through the list and prints each name.
The next block of code checks the password before opening the account.
near_miss: This section of prose moves through the story and introduces each character.
The next part of the essay checks the argument before reaching the conclusion.
tests.basis: Extremely vague label that could cover almost any phrase or any section of code.

tests.label: assignments and initializations in code
should_fire: The code assigns the value five to the counter and initializes it to zero first.
She declared the variable and set it equal to the user's name at startup.
near_miss: The code reads the value five from the counter and displays it to zero first.
She described the variable and compared it to the user's name at startup.
tests.basis: Specific programming construct of assignment and initialization with distinctive verbs and structure.

tests.label: the presence of JSON or structured data format indicators
should_fire: The response came back as {"name": "Ana", "age": 31} in the server log.
He saved the settings in JSON format with keys for theme and language.
near_miss: The response came back as a short note about Ana in the server log.
He saved the settings in plain sentences with notes for theme and language.
tests.basis: Specific structured-data format with concrete indicators like braces, quoted keys, and JSON itself.

tests.label: technical language related to medical studies and procedures
should_fire: Patients in the clinical trial received the treatment twice daily for six weeks.
The surgeon performed the procedure and monitored the patient's recovery afterward.
near_miss: Students in the cooking class received the recipe twice weekly for six weeks.
The teacher performed the demonstration and monitored the students' progress afterward.
tests.basis: Broad medical register covering many studies, treatments, and procedures rather than a narrow pattern.
